dataset.name: ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge (Kelvins)
dataset.description: Conjunction Data Messages (CDMs) received by ESA's Space Debris Office for its satellites, anonymised.
dataset.note: The official test set was hand-picked to over-represent high-risk events (6.9% vs ~1% in the eligible training events), so Brier scores and calibration differ between the two evaluations.

task.target: risk (log10) in the last CDM of the event
task.eligibility: training events need >= 1 CDM at >= 2 days and a final CDM within 2 days of TCA

split.rule: by event, stratified on high-risk: 60% train / 20% validation (all choices) / 20% held-out test (reporting only)

models.baseline: Latest risk prediction: final risk = risk of the latest CDM at least 2 days from TCA; high-risk if that risk >= -6.
models.full: HistGradientBoosting; isotonic-calibrated classifier + two regressors of the change from the latest risk: one over all events, one trained only on high-risk events and used for flagged events (shrunk toward the baseline by a cross-validated weight).
models.live: Same model families restricted to the inputs our live screener produces (see feature_mapping).

thresholds.rule: highest probability that still catches ≥ 95% of the high-risk VALIDATION events

feature_mapping.kelvins: time_to_tca [days] of the latest CDM ≥ 2 d out
feature_mapping.live: (TCA − now) in days; below 2 d the model is outside its training range

feature_mapping.kelvins: risk (ESA's log10 collision probability, full covariance)
feature_mapping.live: log10(Pc) from our screener (isotropic assumed σ), floored at −30
combined isotropic σ (km); identical formula when σ is isotropic
object_type of the other object (official Space-Track type)

operating_point.rule: threshold chosen on the validation split for ≥ 95% recall on high-risk events

lead_time.method: inputs truncated to CDMs at least L days before TCA; same events (those with such a CDM), same targets and thresholds

class_imbalance.before: not handled: unweighted classifier, isotonic calibration
class_imbalance.tried: class_weight='balanced' trees, then isotonic recalibration on unweighted held-out folds
class_imbalance.selection: lower validation Brier score (calibration error also shown)

radial_feature.rule: kept only if the validation Brier score is not worse

all_vs_all_estimate.basis: est.: measured 1 h slice of an all-vs-all cKDTree screen (query_pairs per 60 s step), scaled to 72 h; serial, one core

decision_levels.method: Pc = 10^risk of the latest ESA CDM at least 2 days before TCA; miss = its miss_distance; AI = live model on the same CDM. Truth: final risk ≥ 1e-6. ESA CDMs carry no TLE age, so the stale-data rule never fires. GO also needs a valid avoidance plan, which cannot be checked on historical data; without one GO becomes WATCH, so 'WATCH or above' counts every GO or WATCH trigger.

levels.early_flag: AI early flag: P(high-risk) ≥ the 95%-recall threshold (tag only)
levels.watch_or_above: WATCH or above under the two-stage rule
levels.previous_rule: For comparison: the previous rule (AI flag alone, or Pc / AI final risk ≥ 1e-5, raised WATCH)

method.split: the same events as the trees (60/20/20 by event, seed 42); inputs only CDMs >= 2 days before TCA; target: final risk >= 1e-6
method.lstm: per-CDM linear+ReLU projection -> 1-layer LSTM (64 units, packed variable-length sequences, max 17 CDMs) -> MLP head on [final hidden state, latest CDM]; Adam, BCE, up to 40 epochs
method.calibration: as the trees: 5-fold cross-fitting on the training events, isotonic on each left-out fold, 5 calibrated models averaged
method.selection: LSTM class weighting and epochs by validation PR-AUC; every alert threshold on validation (>= 95% recall)
method.baseline: latest risk; Brier from its hard yes/no (risk >= 1e-6); recall/false alerts at its own 95%-recall threshold on validation; PR-AUC ranks by latest risk

inputs.lstm_full: every numeric CDM column + object type + mission (one-hot), per CDM
inputs.lstm_live: per CDM, the live model's inputs: miss_distance_m, relative_speed_ms, time_to_tca_d, log10_pc, sigma_km, miss_over_sigma, object_type, radial_sep_m

model_comparison.live_rule: the LSTM replaces the live trees only if its live-input version beats them on validation Brier AND PR-AUC
model_comparison.reason: Validation (live inputs): trees Brier 0.00912, PR-AUC 0.219; LSTM Brier 0.00942, PR-AUC 0.201. The LSTM is not better on both, so the trees stay live.
